hu_5.name: The spring of forty-eight
hu_5.brief: The honvéd army needs equipping. Gather seven hundred gold to fill the war chest.

kaloz_sb_3.name: The partner who took the ship
kaloz_sb_3.brief: Blackbeard came as his guest and ended up putting his own men aboard the Revenge. Bonnet stayed in his cabin, reading. Earn six hundred gold by your own hand.

es_4.name: The discovery of paradise
es_4.brief: Thirty-three days on open water, then the birds that mark the shore. Dense wooded islands, hardly any gold. Pitch the first camp: twelve buildings.

es_2.name: The taking of Granada
es_2.brief: The last Moorish stronghold on the peninsula. Break the defenders, and eight hundred years of reconquest come to a close.

kaloz_bb_5.name: The island of Ocracoke
kaloz_bb_5.brief: Only someone who knows the channel runs into that shallow bay. The crew gathers here — and so does the Virginia governor’s squadron. Forty enemies must be broken.

hu_1.name: Belgrade
hu_1.brief: The gate of the southern marches. Build six farms: under siege, food is worth more than the sword.

fr_1.name: The royal domain
fr_1.brief: Louis XI weaves with the patience of a spider. Start with the land: six farms.

kaloz_ns_1.name: The Code of the Brotherhood
kaloz_ns_1.brief: The war is over and the sailors are out of work. In the harbour of Nassau we wrote a code: shared plunder, an elected captain. Build six farms — freedom has to be fed.

kaloz_bb_2.name: Terror as a weapon
kaloz_bb_2.brief: He wove burning fuses into his beard so as to board in smoke and flame. The rumour arrives before the ship: destroy twenty enemy units.

kaloz_sb_4.name: Pardon and turncoat
kaloz_sb_4.brief: He took the pardon, then returned to piracy as “Mister Thomas” — renaming the ship the Royal James. Twenty enemy units must be broken.

pl_3.name: Winged hussars
pl_3.brief: The most feared cavalry in the world is yours. Sweep the enemy away in a single charge.

de_1.name: The order of the empire
de_1.brief: Scattered principalities. Start with the foundations: six farms for the daily bread.

kaloz_ns_6.name: The iron cage
kaloz_ns_6.brief: In the harbour of Port Royal an iron cage waits for everyone who stayed true to the code. If this is the end, make it worthy: break the enemy’s power.

gb_5.name: The trade of the empire
gb_5.brief: Where the ships go, the gold goes too. Gather eight hundred gold.

ru_4.name: Peter the Great’s reform
ru_4.brief: We are cutting a window onto Europe. The fleet and the city need gold: eight hundred.

kaloz_sb_5.name: The Cape Fear river
kaloz_sb_5.brief: He was repairing the ship in the river mouth when Colonel Rhett found him. Five hours of gunfire among the sandbars — thirty enemies must be withstood.

kaloz_bb_6.name: Lieutenant Maynard
kaloz_bb_6.brief: It took five shots and twenty cuts to bring him down — his head was lashed to the bowsprit. If this is the last battle, leave nothing of the enemy standing.

kaloz_bb_3.name: The blockade of Charleston
kaloz_bb_3.brief: For a week he closed the harbour, and instead of ransom he demanded a chest of medicine. Take eight hundred gold from the town.

es_5.name: The first colony
es_5.brief: The palisade of La Navidad stands, but the islanders press us ever harder. Hold out for five minutes.

es_3.name: The port of Palos
es_3.brief: The westward route calls for ships. Build a harbour and gather six hundred gold to fit out the three caravels.

pl_4.name: The relief of Vienna
pl_4.brief: Sobieski comes down from the Kahlenberg. Christian Europe is watching you — hold out for five minutes.

fr_5.name: The Grande Armée
fr_5.brief: Napoleon’s army is on the march. The emperor does not know the word “enough”.

at_6.name: The Great War
at_6.brief: The last summer of the old world. Lead the monarchy into the twentieth century.

gb_6.name: The longest day
gb_6.brief: The island has held. Now lead your empire into the twentieth century.

kaloz_ns_3.name: The letter of pardon
kaloz_ns_3.brief: Woodes Rogers has arrived with the king’s pardon. Whoever takes it walks free — whoever refuses hangs. Beat back the blockade: twenty enemy units.

pl_5.name: Kościuszko’s uprising
pl_5.brief: Scythe-bearing peasants stand beside the nobles. You recruit from the estate, without a barracks.

es_1.name: The Catholic Monarchs
es_1.brief: Ferdinand and Isabella united the crowns. The land comes first: build six farms to supply the Granada campaign.

de_5.name: Blood and iron
de_5.brief: Bismarck’s word: the great questions of the age are not settled by speeches. Break the resistance.

ru_2.name: The walls of the Kremlin
ru_2.brief: Stone upon stone: let twenty buildings stand before winter comes.

fr_2.name: The end of the Hundred Years’ War
fr_2.brief: The English are being pushed off the continent. Scatter what is left of their army.

fr_4.name: Vauban’s fortresses
fr_4.brief: We defend the border with stone, not blood. Build twenty buildings along the line of defence.

es_6.name: Lord of the New World
es_6.brief: Either the island is ours, or we are pushed into the sea. Break the islanders’ resistance.

fr_6.name: The republic
fr_6.brief: Emperors came and went; the nation remained. Step into the twentieth century.

pl_1.name: The land of the Jagiellons
pl_1.brief: The land around Kraków is rich. Build six farms so there is food through the long winter.

kaloz_sb_2.name: The Revenge
kaloz_sb_2.brief: Ten guns, seventy men, and a captain who could not sail. The crew laughed in his face. Build eight buildings to earn some standing.

kaloz_bb_1.name: Queen Anne’s Revenge
kaloz_bb_1.brief: A captured French slave ship became the most feared frigate in the Caribbean. Build up the base: the crew needs six farms.

at_2.name: The siege of Vienna
at_2.brief: The sultan’s army stands beneath the walls. Hold out for five minutes until the relief force arrives.

pl_2.name: The Teutonic Order
pl_2.brief: An armoured wedge is coming from the north. Hold the line for four minutes.

at_5.name: The Compromise
at_5.brief: The empire has become dual. Build twenty buildings — order shows in stone as well.

ru_3.name: The Time of Troubles
ru_3.brief: Pretenders and foreign armies. Hold out for five minutes until order returns.

hu_6.name: The age of machines
hu_6.brief: The world has changed: steel, oil and aircraft. Lead your empire into the twentieth century.

de_6.name: The united empire
de_6.brief: Out of the principalities a nation has grown. Step into the twentieth century.

at_1.name: The Habsburg inheritance
at_1.brief: What others gain by war, you gain by marriage. But food comes first: six farms.

kaloz_ns_4.name: The burning ship
kaloz_ns_4.brief: Vane set fire to a captured French ship and sent it into the blockade. Break out in the confusion: build eight buildings in the free port.

fr_3.name: Versailles
fr_3.brief: The Sun King’s court demands gold. Gather eight hundred gold.

at_4.name: The war of succession
at_4.brief: Maria Theresa’s throne is shaking. War costs money: eight hundred gold for the war chest.

ru_6.name: Industrial great power
ru_6.brief: The empire is building factories. Step into the twentieth century.

kaloz_sb_6.name: The gallows at Charleston
kaloz_sb_6.brief: The gentleman pirate begged for mercy and held a posy of flowers under the gallows. The end of the story is written — but you may finish it differently.

kaloz_sb_1.name: The planter from Barbados
kaloz_sb_1.brief: Bonnet was a wealthy landowner who out of boredom BOUGHT a ship rather than taking one — and paid his crew wages. Start with the estate: six farms.

ru_5.name: Scorched earth
ru_5.brief: The enemy has driven deep. Winter and distance are on our side.

hu_2.name: The long winter
hu_2.brief: The Turkish raids do not cease. Hold the castle for four minutes — whoever endures, wins.

ru_1.name: The rise of Moscow
ru_1.brief: The Tatar yoke is over. Build six farms for the harvest of the frozen land.

kaloz_bb_4.name: The prize run aground
kaloz_bb_4.brief: Queen Anne’s Revenge ran aground — many say on purpose, so the captain could be rid of too large a crew. Rebuild the fleet: ten buildings.

de_2.name: The Landsknecht regiments
de_2.brief: Mercenaries are expensive but unshakeable. Scatter the neighbour’s army.

gb_4.name: The New Model Army
gb_4.brief: Cromwell’s disciplined regiments do not know flight. Break the royalists.

gb_1.name: After the roses
gb_1.brief: The civil war is over and the country is exhausted. Six farms, so there is something to eat.

kaloz_ns_2.name: The harbour of the republic
kaloz_ns_2.brief: A free port only survives if it has something to sell. Build a harbour and a market, and gather six hundred gold.

hu_4.name: Rákóczi’s war of independence
hu_4.brief: “Cum Deo pro Patria et Libertate.” The kuruc take up arms. Scatter the imperial forces.

hu_3.name: The Black Army
hu_3.brief: Matthias’s mercenaries come not from a barracks but from the royal treasury. You recruit from the headquarters.

pl_6.name: The liberation of Warsaw
pl_6.brief: The capital lies in ruins, but it is not silent. Rebuild the country on the threshold of the twentieth century.

gb_2.name: The age of the archers
gb_2.brief: The longbow is still the most fearsome weapon. Prove it on the battlefield.

de_4.name: Prussian discipline
de_4.brief: The Great Elector is building a standing army. Twenty buildings, in soldierly order.

de_3.name: The Thirty Years’ War
de_3.brief: Half of Europe is ablaze. Hold out for five minutes — this war is not about the swift.

at_3.name: The Holy League
at_3.brief: Eugene of Savoy leads the imperial army. Break the enemy’s strength along the Danube.

gb_3.name: The Armada
gb_3.brief: The threat comes from the sea. Hold out for five minutes; the storm is your ally.

kaloz_ns_5.name: The captain voted down
kaloz_ns_5.brief: The code has turned against you: the crew accuse you of cowardice. Prove them wrong — destroy thirty-five enemy units.
